subject: SLA deviation request — customer-controlled edge latency and telemetry responsibilities
messages:

Subject: Request for operational carveout — customer-managed edge peering

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we described, Lorica is running a hybrid inference gateway in our colo (managed by our network team) that performs TLS termination and traffic shaping before it hits the Redwood private deployment. Over the last two quarters we've observed intermittent 80–300ms tail latency spikes that we can trace to our WAN / provider-peering handoff.

Because that infrastructure is customer-controlled, we need Redwood to acknowledge an operational carveout in the Private deployment SLA that excludes outages/latency caused by:
- our colo transit / peering (third-party ISP events)
- our on-prem NAT/transit maintenance windows
- misconfigurations inside our edge gateway

Can you confirm the process to request an exception and what evidence you need to accept an attribution carveout? I've attached a short packet of traces and timestamps from last week for reference.

We are happy to:
- provide packet captures & signed runbook access for agreed windows
- add a dedicated peering arrangement if required (subject to costs/lead times)

Tim
Tim Grant
Head of Platform Engineering | Lorica Therapeutics

Tim — thanks for the details and the traces. I’ve pulled the packet samples and a quick read shows clear handoff jitter correlated to the timestamps you called out.

Short answers up front:
1) We can process a limited SLA deviation for customer-controlled edge/network faults, but we need: 
   - reproducible evidence (captures + timestamps + correlation to Redwood request IDs),
   - a signed mutual action plan (MAP) that defines responsibilities and runbook access for incident triage, and
   - telemetry hooks (span/request ids in the ingress) so Redwood can reliably attribute latency.
2) For contractual language, we typically add a narrow "Customer-Controlled Network" carveout to the availability/latency section and include a telemetry/evidence clause.

Can you confirm the runbook access scope your network team can give (read-only packet captures vs. full debug access) and whether Lorica can stand up a peering link (BGP) if we require it for isolation?

Priyom / Vivek — looping you in to scope a proposed amendment and quick technical checklist. If we can get their runbook and a few more traces, I’ll draft proposed wording.

-Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Sales (Private deployments) | Redwood Inference

Rohan — see my initial tech notes below. I reviewed the packet samples and the trace_metadata.csv. Two quick points before legal:

1) Attribution checklist (minimum):
   • Request IDs: we need the inbound request IDs (Redwood token/trace) correlated with timestamps.
   • Ingress spans: add an X-Redwood-Trace header at the gateway so we can tie client-side latencies to server-side token consumption.
   • Bounded window: pick an agreed maintenance window for us to run correlation tests (we recommend three 24hr windows).

2) Possible mitigations:
   • Dedicated peering (BGP) between Lorica colo and Redwood edge (cost + 6–8 week lead).
   • Establish an eBPF-based sampling agent on their gateway to capture 0.1% of flows with trace ids.
   • Runbook & access: read-only packet captures + time-synced logging should be sufficient for most attributions.

Kimberly / Legal: if we accept an attribution carveout, legally we propose a narrowly-scoped clause: 1) define "Customer-Controlled Network Events", 2) require evidence per checklist, 3) include a remediation/Audit window and 4) offer an opt-in dedicated-peering SLA upgrade path that narrows the carveout.

I attached a draft amendment (proposed_sla_amendment_v1.docx) and a sample technical checklist. Happy to iterate.

--Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request for operational carveout — customer-controlled edge peering

Tim — thanks for the traces and for being proactive about remediation options. We reviewed internally with engineering and legal and propose the following path forward: 

1) What we need from Lorica to accept a narrow SLA deviation:
   - The inbound Redwood request IDs for the attached traces (so we can fully correlate).
   - Confirmation of read-only runbook access and a point contact for on-call triage during the three test windows.
   - Agreement to install a lightweight trace header (X-Redwood-Trace) on the gateway or to include the Redwood token as a passthrough header.

2) Proposed contractual amendment (summary):
   • Add a new section "Customer-Controlled Network Events" that excludes outages and latency caused solely by network elements under the customer's control, provided the customer: (a) provides attributable evidence per the checklist, and (b) cooperates with Redwood's triage process within the agreed window.
   • Provide an "Availability Reassessment" clause: if Lorica implements dedicated peering and the telemetry configuration above for 30 days, Redwood will re-evaluate and may reduce the carveout scope.

3) Next steps & timelines:
   - Can Lorica provide the missing Redwood request ids and confirm runbook access by EOD Friday (2027-11-05)?
   - If yes, we will finalize the amendment and route for signatures (we will try to keep changes to a single short appendix).

I’ve attached the draft amendment and highlighted the new clauses. If Legal needs different wording, we can iterate quickly — this is intended to be a narrow, evidence-driven carveout rather than a broad SLA reduction.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30 minute call Monday to walk legal / ops through the checklist.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts & Compliance | Redwood Inference
